en: Using an inclined plane like a wooden ramp reduces the force needed to move heavy boxes, preventing back injuries.
Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction on wet bathroom tiles, preventing dangerous slips and falls.
Storing heavy objects on lower shelves prevents gravity from pulling them down onto your head if they fall.
Keeping strong neodymium magnets away from smartphones prevents the magnetic field from damaging the phone's internal electronic components.
Never touching electrical switches with wet hands prevents electric shock because water is a good conductor of electricity.
Wearing sunglasses with UV protection during sunny recess blocks harmful light rays and prevents long-term retina damage.
Wearing earplugs near loud karaoke machines reduces sound energy intensity, protecting your eardrums from permanent hearing damage.
Using a dry cloth pot holder when lifting a hot pan blocks heat conduction and prevents severe hand burns.
Eating a banana before playing basketball provides your body with stored chemical energy to fuel your muscle movements.
Unplugging appliances by pulling the hard plastic plug instead of the cord prevents wire damage and electrical fires.
Using a battery-powered flashlight during a power outage prevents the fire hazards associated with lighting open-flame candles.
Applying lubricating oil to a rusty bicycle chain reduces harmful friction, preventing the chain from snapping and causing crashes.
